name: Google Ads
blurb: Search, PMax and Shopping builds, RSAs, keywords and negatives, bidding, conversion tracking, audits and the Ads API.
searches: Google Ads new feature announcement Performance Max AI Max
Google Ads API release notes new version GAQL
Google Ads Smart Bidding change negative keywords update
Enhanced Conversions Consent Mode Data Manager API update
agent skill Google Ads Claude MCP

tests.prompt: Build a Google Search campaign for a plumbing company in Leeds that wants emergency call-outs and boiler repair bookings. Budget £1,500 a month. Give the structure, keywords with match types, one RSA per ad group, and assets.
tests.good: Brand and non-brand split with separate budgets; tight ad groups by service; phrase/exact keywords with Presence location targeting around Leeds; Search only (partners/Display off); 15 headlines ≤30 and 4 descriptions ≤90 with counts shown; call asset and sitelinks/callouts within limits; Maximize Conversions start; conversion tracking (calls and bookings) flagged as a prerequisite; no unsupported claims.

tests.prompt: Here is my search terms export for last 30 days (pasted CSV with term, clicks, cost, conversions). Find wasted spend and give me negatives and new keywords.
tests.good: Uses the export's conversion column; states disclosed vs total clicks; harvest/negate/move diff with match type and level per negative; n-gram cost table; break-even CVR or sample-size check before calling relevant terms waste; overblocking review; no invented negatives beyond the data; nothing applied without approval.

tests.prompt: Our Google Ads conversions dropped 40% this week but spend is flat. What happened and what should we do?
tests.good: Confirms the drop over complete days vs an equal prior window; splits by conversion action, campaign and device; checks tag/consent/landing page and offline upload health; checks change history (30-day limit) and conversion lag; separates tracking failure from real demand change; warns against pausing or re-bidding during diagnosis; gives a verification plan.

tests.prompt: Launch Google Search ads for our UK payroll software for accountancy firms (£4,000 a month, goal: demo requests). Our demo page converts at 1.1%, so fix it to match the ads, and give the sales team a weekly dashboard of leads and cost per demo.
tests.good: States a short plan first: the build here (conversion-tracking.md first, then campaign-build.md, keywords-negatives.md, ad-copy-assets.md, bidding-budgets.md), the page through website-building (plan-and-copy.md, performance-cwv.md: headline echoes the ad and the query, one CTA, fast on mobile), the dashboard through data-analysis (dashboards-kpis.md: cost per demo defined with numerator, denominator and window). Fires a test demo conversion before launch; splits brand from non-brand; phrase and exact match with Maximize Conversions to start; RSA lines with counts shown; no change applied without an approved diff; checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: About a third of the 2,400 products in our Shopify store show as disapproved or limited in Google Merchant Center, mostly 'price mismatch' and 'missing GTIN', and our Shopping campaign spend has dropped. Find out which products and why through the Merchant API, fix what can be fixed without touching the Shopify catalogue, and tell me what to do on the Google Ads side.
tests.good: Works through the Merchant API, not the Content API for Shopping, which was sunset on 18 Aug 2026; mentions linking a Google Cloud project to the Merchant Center account with developer registration and a service account or OAuth credential with minimal scope; groups the product issues by type with counts (aggregate product statuses and product issues) and separates account-level issues from product-level ones; fixes price mismatch at the source (Shopify price, sale price or currency versus the landing page, automatic item updates settings) and handles missing GTIN with a supplemental data source linked to the primary feed, not edits to Shopify, and does not invent GTINs or set identifierExists wrongly; on the Ads side checks Shopping/PMax impressions and spend by product group against the disapproved set, does not change bids or budgets while products are disapproved, and re-checks after re-review; shows the exact supplemental data source or feed rows for approval before anything is created or fetched live, and keeps credentials out of chat.

tools.name: Google Ads Editor
tools.why: Free official desktop bulk-editing app that every 2026 PPC tool round-up (Optmyzr, WASK, Swydo, Ryze) lists first or second; the standard way to import a campaign build CSV and review changes before posting.

tools.name: Google Ads API
tools.why: The programmatic interface agencies and in-house teams use for reporting, bulk changes and tooling; v25 shipped 2026-07-22 per the official release notes, and the official Google Ads MCP server (1,000+ GitHub stars) wraps it.

tools.name: Google Keyword Planner
tools.why: The free, first-party source of search volume ranges, top-of-page bids and forecasts inside every Google Ads account; named in the 2026 PPC tool round-ups and exposed in the API as KeywordPlanIdeaService.

tools.name: Google Tag Manager
tools.why: The default way to deploy the Google tag, conversion tags and Consent Mode on client sites; Google publishes a Tag Manager API and several community GTM MCP servers exist (Stape's has 226 stars).

tools.name: Google Analytics 4
tools.why: The measurement layer almost every Google Ads account links to for key events and audiences; Google ships an official Analytics MCP (3,300+ stars) and official Data API and Admin API skills.

tools.name: Google Merchant Center
tools.why: Required for every Shopping and product-feed-driven Performance Max campaign; the Content API for Shopping was sunset on 2026-08-18 and replaced by the Merchant API, and Google now offers an alpha Merchant API MCP endpoint.

tools.name: Looker Studio
tools.why: The free dashboard tool most agencies and in-house teams use for recurring Google Ads plus GA4 reporting (top of the Swydo, Pace Ads and Ryze reporting round-ups); it has no MCP or conversational API, only the Linking API, Looker Studio API and community connectors.

tools.name: Google Ads Scripts
tools.why: Browser-based JavaScript automation inside Google Ads used by agencies for alerts, budget pacing and Sheets reports with no server; Brainlabs' open-source collection has 160 stars and wookstar ships a skill.

tools.name: Data Manager API
tools.why: Google's unified ingestion API for offline and enhanced conversions and Customer Match across Google Ads and GA4, with three official Google skills.

tools.name: Optmyzr
tools.why: Ranked first in Optmyzr's own and several third-party 2026 PPC tool round-ups for agencies; its official MCP is in Claude's connector directory and can add keywords and negatives behind a mandatory preview.

tools.name: Supermetrics
tools.why: The standard connector that pipes Google Ads into Sheets, Looker Studio, Excel, Power BI and BigQuery for agency reporting (Swydo and Ryze round-ups); its MCP is in Claude's connector directory.

tools.name: Semrush
tools.why: Most-cited competitor PPC research tool (keywords competitors bid on, ad copy history, estimated spend) in the 2026 round-ups; has an official Claude connector and a paid API-unit API.

tools.name: Microsoft Advertising
tools.why: The usual second search platform; accounts commonly import Google Ads campaigns, and the legacy SOAP API is deprecated on 2027-01-31 in favour of REST per Microsoft's docs.

tools.name: Adalysis
tools.why: PPC audit and ad-testing platform listed in the Optmyzr and WASK round-ups, with an Adalysis MCP for Claude.

tools.name: CallRail
tools.why: Market leader in call tracking: Datanyze ranks it #1 with 30.87% share and 52,000+ companies (Google's own call conversion tracking is #2 at 27.78%), and 2026 Google Ads call-tracking round-ups list it as the SMB/agency default for keyword-level call attribution via gclid capture and Google Ads conversion import; calls are a primary conversion for local lead-gen accounts.

tools.name: Opteo
tools.why: Named alongside Optmyzr, Google Ads Editor and TrueClicks as a top Google Ads tool in Optmyzr's and TheOptimizer's 2026 round-ups and widely used by freelancers and small agencies (plans from $129/month); its official OAuth MCP (https://api.opteo.com/mcp) reads and, after confirmation, changes accounts. The earlier 'no MCP' reason is out of date.

tools.name: SpyFu
tools.why: The PPC-specialist competitor research tool (15+ years of competitors' Google Ads keywords, ad copy history and estimated spend, from $29/month), named with Semrush as the top Google Ads competitor research tools in the 2026 round-ups; has a bearer-key REST API (PPC Research, Ad History, Kombat) but no MCP.

tools.name: Google Ads Transparency Center
tools.why: Google's free, official library of every ad a verified advertiser runs on Search, Display, YouTube and Gmail, filterable by date and region; the standard free way to read competitors' live RSAs before writing copy or building competitor campaigns, cited in every 2026 competitor-research round-up.
